findings.title: Camera corner blind spot: at diagonal orbits neither shell wall cuts away and the full-height outer wall fills the screen, hiding Pip completely
findings.problem: The cutaway in src/game.ts:385 decides per wall with `wall.normal.dot(toCam)>.2`, where toCam is the direction from the wall's CENTRE (its parent's world position) to the camera. When the camera orbits to a diagonal yaw behind a corner, the direction from the far-away centre of one wall comes out almost parallel to that wall. Its dot product drops below 0.2, so the wall stays 3 m tall even though it is the wall right between the camera and Pip. In shot -81 (Pip at about (5.9,-4.6) next to the claw cabinet, camera orbited to yaw ≈2.43 so it sits outside the south-east corner at about (11,-10.7)), the whole 1440×900 frame is the beige outside face of the east wall. Pip, the room and the cabinets are all invisible. That is a reachable state for any player who right-drags the camera toward a back corner. Good Job's number-one complaint was the camera; AGENTS 8 promises an orbit camera that never loses the player. It also breaks DR-75, which says cutaways must follow the camera direction and orbiting must never show the wrong face.
findings.fix: In src/game.ts updateCamera, replace the centre-based test with a test against the segment from the camera to Pip. For each shell wall, compute the signed distance of the camera and of Pip to the wall's plane (the plane through `at` with normal `wall.normal`). Stub the wall when the camera is on the outside (d_cam>0) and Pip is on the inside (d_pip<0). As a cheap fallback, also stub any wall whose centre-dot test is >-0.1 while the camera is outside its plane. Keep the 0.15 lerp. Also clamp camera distance so the camera never ends up more than ~0.5 m behind a full-height wall: raycast the camera→focus line against the walls and pull in.
findings.verify: Rerun mockups/review5/tools/arcade-models/s9.mjs and retake arcade-models-81: Pip and the claw/handheld cabinets must be visible. Add a sweep: at 4 room corners × 8 yaws at zoom 9 and 38, assert that ≥70% of a Pip-ID render or a raycast to Pip's head, chest and feet is unobstructed by shell walls.
findings.verify_reason: Reproduced it with verify-arcade-models/v1.mjs. I walked to (5.9,-4.6), zoomed in, then orbited (-262,-150) and (-120,0). The camera settles at (10.01,2.76,-9.34) and the whole frame is beige wall; it does not clear even after one more second (verify-arcade-models-04-corner-blind-settled.jpg, same as arcade-models-81). Rays from the camera to Pip's feet, chest and head all hit a WALL_UP (#efe2c8) mesh at (8.97,y,-8.13). That is the BACK shell wall (z=-8, normal [0,-1], decor.ts:73), not the east wall: the arcade has no east shell wall. The math matches the claimed mechanism: the vector from the wall centre (0,-8) to the camera normalizes to (0.991,-0.133), and its dot with the normal is 0.133, below 0.2 (game.ts:385), so the wall stays full height. The same bug happens on the west side wall. In v1 B, the camera ends at (-11.85,3.67,5.83), dot 0.144, and the full-height west wall hides Pip's body (verify-arcade-models-06). It is recoverable by orbiting back, so P1, not P0.
extra_evidence: mockups/review5/tools/verify-arcade-models/v1.mjs (A2/A3: cam 10.01,2.76,-9.34, all 3 rays hit #efe2c8 at z -8.13; B1: cam -11.85,3.67,5.83)
src/levels/decor.ts:73 (only back [0,-1] and side [-1,0] shell walls)
findings.fix_correction: The fix direction is right: stub the wall when the camera is outside its plane and Pip is inside. The simplest form is `stub = wallPlaneSignedDist(cam) > 0` (camera outside the plane), with no dot test against the centre direction. Leave out the 'pull the camera in' raycast: the room is designed as a dollhouse cutaway, so stubbing is enough. The title and evidence should say back wall / west side wall, not east wall.

findings.title: Storeroom half-walls (1.35 m) and arcade cabinets (2.16 m) are not occluders: they hide Pip on the main tray route and between cabinets
findings.problem: The tray route (tests/station-arcade.spec.ts toBench: (-5.5,6.6)→(-7.2,5.8)→(-8.3,4.4)) runs right along the storeroom's east half-wall store-b (x -6.55..-6.25, z 2.45..5.4, h 1.35). That wall is built by interiorWall() (src/levels/decor.ts:44-48), which never registers with game.occluders. Only pillars do (decor.ts:55). With the camera orbited west of the storeroom (shot -50, settled 20 frames), the wall cap and face fill the lower two thirds of the screen and only Pip's hat shows. ART research-art-12 recorded this as 'cuts Pip off at the waist'; it is now worse at zoom 9. The same happens with every arcade cabinet, which is 2.16 m tall and 1 m wide: from the east-wall side (shots -24, -52), Pip standing among the right-wall cabinets is hidden behind blank cabinet backs, with only a sliver visible, and nothing fades. Since every one of the 12 cabinets is a solid() fixed body with toon materials, the occlusion ray (game.ts:387) never sees them.
findings.fix: (1) interiorWall(): clone the lower and upper materials per wall, set transparent=true and push each wall mesh into game.occluders, as decor.ts:55 does for pillars. (2) cabinet() in room.ts and buildCabinet() in station.ts: give each cabinet group a single invisible proxy box (1×2.2×0.9), add it to occluders, and when it is hit, drive the opacity of the cabinet's parts. Simpler: collect the cabinet's toon parts in a per-cabinet cloned material set and fade them together. (3) Cast 3 rays (feet p.y-.6, chest p.y+.4, head p.y+1.0) instead of the single ray at game.ts:387, and fade to 0.25 as DR-12 requires (today 0.15 at only one ray height). Use alpha-hash or dither to keep sorting stable (DR-78).
findings.verify: Retake arcade-models-50 (s5.mjs 'west-wall-orbit') and -24/-52: the half-wall and cabinets between camera and Pip fade to ≤0.25 opacity within 0.2 s, and Pip is ≥70% visible. Add a spec that walks the toBench route at 8 yaws and checks the occluder opacities.
findings.verify_reason: Half of this finding is wrong. The storeroom half-wall part is REFUTED. interiorWall() at src/levels/decor.ts:44-48 clones a transparent material per part and pushes every part into game.occluders. git blame dates that to 65a7344 (Sep 29), and the DR-12 'Known' line about it is stale. At runtime in v1 B, a CAP_DARK (#8e5a36) occluder from store-b is faded to 0.15. Shot -50 / my -06 is the shell-wall cutaway bug from finding 0: the camera is at x -11.85, outside the west wall at x -11, and the feet ray hits the shell-wall cap at (-10.98,3.18,5.71). It is not store-b. The cabinet part is CONFIRMED. cabinet() (room.ts:59-69) uses plain toon materials in game.root and is never added to occluders. In v1 C (camera behind the hopper at (14.31,3.67,-3.93)), the feet and chest rays both hit the hopper body #ffb38a at opacity 1, and Pip is hidden except for his hat (verify-arcade-models-07-hopper-behind.jpg, same as arcade-models-24). Shot -52, however, shows Pip mostly visible between cabinets, so that example is overstated. The fix's claim that DR-12 needs 0.25 'today 0.15' is also backwards: 0.15 already meets ≤0.25.
extra_evidence: v1.mjs C1: feet/chest rays hit #ffb38a hopper body at d 4.7-4.9 m, opacity 1
findings.fix_correction: Drop step (1): the interior walls already fade. Keep step (2), making cabinets occluders with per-cabinet cloned transparent materials, or a proxy box whose hit fades the cabinet parts. Keep step (3), adding feet and head rays to game.ts:387, but leave the target opacity at 0.15, which already satisfies DR-12's ≤0.25. Shot -50 is fixed by finding 0, not by this one.

findings.title: REGRESSION: draw calls rose to ~1500 at the start view (A13 was 1181); station machinery and 12 cabinets are not merged
findings.problem: `snap().drawCalls` is 1497 at the start view and 1488 in the survey (s1.mjs), and 1022 at a zoomed view (s9.mjs). DR-24 allows about 250, and review 3 B N9 / A13 recorded 1181, so this is a regression. A scene traverse (s8.mjs) shows where it comes from. The bench's `top` group holds 221 separate meshes: 16 bin blocks of 7 meshes each, plus bin walls, pads, links, LED, motor and meter. Each of the 12 cabinets has 12–24 meshes and is built straight into game.root (room.ts:83, 94, 95; station.ts:215), not into decorRoot, so freeze() (kit.ts:77) never merges them. The tray's riding blocks are another 48 meshes, and there are 144 loose single meshes. OutlineEffect draws every visible mesh twice. The host GPU holds 60 fps, but on integrated GPUs and phones (NEXT_STEPS asks for a phone bench check) this is the main frame cost. The prop clones are already instanced (125 InstancedMesh), so the cost is almost all station art.
findings.fix: (1) In room.ts, build every cabinet into game.decorRoot, which is frozen and merged at game.ts:105. Keep only the marquee `face` and the `screen` as separate meshes, since light(k) swaps their material. Parent those two to game.root at the cabinet's world transform. (2) In station.ts buildBins(), merge each bin's 4 decorative blocks into one geometry per material: mergeGeometries over blockMesh children, keeping the labels as one merged plane per bin. They never change. (3) Build the bench's static parts (board base, supply posts, pads, rails, meter housing, power box base, sign-off base) into one group and call freeze() on it once after build(). Keep the live parts (LED dome, fuse disc, lever, lamps, posContent, acrossContent, heldMesh) separate. (4) Dispose trayRide after delivery instead of only hiding it. Target ≤300 draw calls at the game camera.
findings.verify: Rerun s1.mjs and s8.mjs: `snap().drawCalls` ≤ 300 at start and in the survey, and the bench `top` group ≤ 60 meshes. Retake arcade-models-36/-38 to confirm the bench looks identical. tests/station-arcade.spec.ts still passes.
findings.verify_reason: I measured it myself (v3.mjs): snap().drawCalls is 1497 at start and 1497 in the survey, the bench top group at (-0.2,1,-2.45) holds 221 meshes, and there are 125 InstancedMesh. The cabinets are built into game.root (room.ts:83, 94, 95; station.ts:215), so freeze(decorRoot) at game.ts:105 never merges them. DR-24 (≤250) is broken by about 6×. Two caveats. Calling it a 'regression' from 1181 is shaky: review 3 counted with 40 props and a different method, and the room now has 132 props plus clutter. And no frame drop on the host was shown, so this is a budget and portability problem, not something that noticeably hurts play today. That makes it P2.
extra_evidence: mockups/review5/tools/verify-arcade-models/v3.mjs output: dc start 1497, survey 1497, topMeshes 221, meshes 651 (420 visible), inst 125
findings.fix_correction: Steps (1) to (3) are sound. When cabinets move to decorRoot, keep the five broken cabinets' face and screen meshes outside the frozen group, because light(k) swaps their materials (room.ts:122-123). The six working cabinets can be frozen completely. Drop step (4): trayRide is already visible=false after delivery (station.ts:360), so it costs no draw calls.

findings.title: The carried resistor tray (and any carried prop) keeps a random tilt: the tray is carried ~70° on edge beside Pip's head
findings.problem: The carry code (src/game.ts:331) drives only the held body's linear velocity toward a point 1.05 m ahead at p.y+0.55 (≈1.32 m) and zeroes the angular velocity each frame. It never restores orientation, so any tilt picked up from a collision while walking stays. On the spec's route from the storeroom to the bench, the tray arrives standing almost on edge at Pip's right shoulder, with its 6 riding resistor blocks still glued to its tilted face (station.ts:369 copies the tray quaternion to trayRide). Shot -32 and crop -32b show this. A carried cone (shots -71, -72) sits tip-first at Pip's face, tilted about 60°. This is the job's one carry beat, and a tray of loose parts carried vertically reads as a physics glitch: the blocks would spill. ART F16 reported this (research-art-46) and it is still open. At pickup (shot -30) the tray also sits beside the head, held by one raised mitt, rather than level at chest height in front of both mitts.
findings.fix: In src/game.ts:331, after setting linvel: build a target quaternion of yaw-only `heading` (setFromAxisAngle(Y, heading)). Slerp the body's rotation toward it, e.g. b.setRotation(q.slerp(target, min(1, dt*12))), or set an angvel proportional to the axis-angle error (×10). Lower the carry height to p.y+0.35 (≈1.12 m, chest) and the distance for light props to 0.6 + size[2]/2, so the item sits between the mitts. For trays, also lock the rotation fully (b.lockRotations(true) while held, restore on drop). Point the arm IK at the item's side edges (two mitts) instead of one raised mitt.
findings.verify: Rerun s4.mjs up to arcade-models-32 and add an assertion: while held, the tray's up vector has y > 0.95 (tilt < 18°) every frame on the toBench route. The crop shows the tray level at chest height between both mitts, not intersecting a 0.3 m sphere around the head at y 1.4.
findings.verify_reason: game.ts:331 sets only linvel toward (ahead 1.05 m, y p.y+.55) and zeroes angvel, so orientation is never restored. trayRide copies the body's quaternion (station.ts:369). I measured it in v2.mjs on the spec route: the tray's up-vector y is 1.00 at pickup, 0.96 to 0.97 after the storeroom, and 0.89 (≈27°) from the middle of the route to the bench, so the tilt stays. I saw 27°, not ~70°; the amount depends on what the tray bumps into. The tray rides at y 1.21–1.30 m, 1.0–1.06 m ahead of Pip, so 'beside the head' is a perspective effect, not contact with the head sphere. Arcade-models-32b shows the edge-on case. This is cosmetic, so P2.
extra_evidence: mockups/review5/tools/verify-arcade-models/v2.mjs: tilt upY along route 0.96..0.97 then 0.89 x12, held tray y 1.21-1.30, dist 1.0-1.06
findings.fix_correction: Locking rotations while held (b.lockRotations(true,true), and setRotation to a yaw-only heading on pickup) is the simplest robust fix; the slerp is not needed. Restore with lockRotations(false) on drop or throw. Lowering to p.y+.35 is fine.

findings.title: The job item is not in the job colour language: the tray is clutter pink (#ff7eb6, the exact first clutter colour) while yellow #ffd84d is spread over clutter boxes, beanbags and chairs
findings.problem: DR-45 says job items share one visual language (yellow #ffc94d/#ffc629 with ink stripes, plus the #ffd84d grab cue) and no decorative clutter uses it. In the arcade, the resistor tray is `color:'#ff7eb6'` (src/levels/arcade.ts:133). That is the same hex as the first entry of the arcade clutter palette (arcade.ts:155 colors), the pink beanbags, the pink chairs (arcade.ts:138) and the pink storeroom boxes (#ffa6c9, arcade.ts:135). Meanwhile LEMON #ffd84d, the grab-cue colour, appears on clutter boxes, beanbags and chairs all over the floor (shots -01, -21, -55, -57). In the start shot the tray is a small pink rectangle on a dark counter, surrounded by pink boxes, a pink storeroom box at the door and pink beanbags. It is not one of the three highest-contrast shapes (DR-43), so the player relies on the marker to find it. The resistor-stock bricks on the storeroom shelf (room.ts:112) are also pink, mint and lilac blocks, the same candy look as the tray's blocks, so a player may try to grab them.
findings.fix: (1) arcade.ts:133: make the tray job yellow `#ffc94d` with an ink rim. In prefabs.ts:156 'tray', add a 2 cm INK lip (four box(.8,.04,.02)/box(.02,.04,.5) rails) and two cut-out handles, so it reads as a carry tray and matches the reel/plug language. (2) arcade.ts:155: drop '#ffd84d' from the clutter colours and replace it with a peach '#ffb38a'. Keep pink, mint, grape and sky for fabrics only (see the DR-51 finding). (3) arcade.ts:138: chairs avoid LEMON. (4) room.ts:112: make the shelf stock read as 'stock bins', not tray blocks: kraft card boxes (#c98f5a) with a small CANDY-coloured value label each.
findings.verify: Retake arcade-models-01: the tray is the only job-yellow prop in frame. A ΔE<25 scan against #ffc94d in the start shot finds only the tray, the marker and the grab cue. Squint and greyscale tests (DR-43) rank the tray in the top 3 local contrasts.
findings.verify_reason: The claim is real but the line numbers are wrong: src/levels/arcade.ts has 31 lines. The tray is '#ff7eb6' at arcade.ts:7, which matches the first clutter colour (arcade.ts:29), the chairs (arcade.ts:12) and the pink beanbag (arcade.ts:13). Storeroom boxes alternate '#ffa6c9' (arcade.ts:9). LEMON '#ffd84d' is in the clutter palette and on chairs. In arcade-models-01 the tray is a small pink rectangle on the counter among pink boxes and beanbags. The yellow marker and the objective text still lead the player to it, so the clarity loss is moderate: P2.
findings.fix_correction: Same fix, applied at arcade.ts:7 (tray colour), arcade.ts:12 and :29 (palettes) and room.ts:112 (shelf stock).

findings.title: False affordance: a grabbable cable reel sits in the storeroom next to the tray in a room with no cable at all
findings.problem: arcade.ts:136 places `{kind:'reel',x:-7.6,z:6.2,color:'#9b7bf0'}` in the storeroom, 1.5 m from the tray's counter and right on the spec route ((-7.2,5.8)). The station room has no cable (game.ts hides the rope in station rooms), yet the prompt shows 'E Grab the cable reel' when Pip walks past (shot -12), and the reel is the most job-looking object in the storeroom (shots -10, -30, -31). In every cable floor the reel is THE job item, so a returning player will pick it up and carry it to the bench, where nothing happens. That breaks 'play by doing': the world offers an action that has no meaning.
findings.fix: Remove the reel from arcade.ts:136, or replace it with a non-job storeroom prop: a 'box' of ticket rolls (kraft #c98f5a) or a 'coolbox'. If a reel is wanted as flavour, make it a fixed decor part (not a prop, no grab prompt), wound with arcade ribbon in grape, mounted on the shelf at y 1.2.
findings.verify: Walk the toBench route (s4.mjs) and log every prompt text: no prompt mentions 'cable' or 'reel' in the arcade. Retake arcade-models-12.
findings.verify_reason: The reel is at arcade.ts:10 (not :136). In v2.mjs, logging prompts while walking the toBench route (-5.5,6.6)→(-7.2,5.8) shows 'Grab the cable reel' on screen. Nothing in game.ts or the station uses a reel in station rooms. The confusion is real, but every clutter prop in the room is grabbable without meaning, so the impact is small: P2.
extra_evidence: mockups/review5/tools/verify-arcade-models/v2.mjs output: 'Grab the cable reel' prompt on the spec route

findings.title: Arcade cabinets have blank backs and flat 1.5 m² sides, and the bench meter has a bare back: they read as pastel slabs from every angle except the front
findings.problem: cabinet() (src/stations/arcade/room.ts:59-69) is a body rbox, a plinth, a tilted head box, a screen, a deck with 3 buttons, a coin door and a marquee, all on the front face. The back and the two sides are plain single-colour faces. Each side is 0.8 m × ~1.9 m ≈ 1.5 m², 3× the DR-62 limit of 0.5 m² untrimmed, and the back is 0.95 × 1.9 m. Since 3 cabinets stand against the east wall facing west and 3 against the west wall, orbiting even 90° shows a row of blank candy slabs: in shots -24 and -52 the right-wall cabinets from behind read as fridges or lockers, not arcade machines. The serviced cabinet (station.ts:216-220), described as 'back open, ribbon cable to the board' in the station.ts:212 comment, has a closed blank back too (shot -71). The bench meter (station.ts:184-187) is a pale pink board with a bare back (shot -34). DR-63 asks that every model has a finished back because the player orbits.
findings.fix: In cabinet(): (a) add T-molding: an INK or PLUM box(.025,1.9,.82) strip on each side's front edge and along the top of the body. (b) Add side art on each side: a flat decal plane (.62×1.1) using a small canvasTex per seed (a star burst or game logo in the cabinet's accent), offset 6 mm. (c) Add back detail: a recessed rear door rbox(.6,1.1,.02) in a darker body shade, two vent grilles (5 × box(.4,.02,.015) INK), a power cord tube from y .2 down to the floor (TubeGeometry r .015, INK). (d) Bevel the head into a slanted marquee hood, so the side silhouette has the classic stepped profile. For the serviced cabinet: actually open the back (omit the rear panel, add a dark interior box and a visible PCB plane in #2f7a5b with the ribbon cable emerging). For the meter: add a back housing rbox(1.5,.9,.06) in PLUM with 4 screw dots and a vent strip.
findings.verify: Zoom-9 orbit sweep at 0/90/180/270° around (9.7,1.2), (-9.9,-1.5) and the bench (s3/s5 scripts). No visible single-colour face >0.5 m² without trim, decal or panel line, and the backs show a door, vents and a cord. Retake arcade-models-24, -52, -71, -34.
findings.verify_reason: cabinet() (room.ts:59-69) puts every detail on the front face. The serviced cabinet (station.ts:215-220) has a closed rbox body even though the comment says 'back open'. The meter body (station.ts:184-187) is a single rbox. Cabinet backs are blank pastel slabs in verify-arcade-models-07, arcade-models-52 and arcade-models-71. This breaks DR-62/DR-63, but it is polish, so P2.

findings.title: Play-tester is still a realistic peg-person human (skin-tone head, brown hair) in a world of Pip plus blobs
findings.problem: station.ts:225-231 builds the kid from blue cylinder legs, an orange cylinder torso, a '#f2c49b' skin sphere head and a brown hair cap, with cylinder arms ending in skin-coloured spheres. It stands at the serviced cabinet, fully visible at the game camera and in every bench approach (shots -19, -33, -35, -18). It is the only humanoid besides Pip and directly contradicts DR-60 (one character language). It also reads stiff: the yellow shirt stripe box(.27,.05,.02) sits on the visible back as a floating plank (shot -35). ART F3 reported this; it is still open.
findings.fix: Replace the kid with a small blob: kit.blobMesh(BLOBC[k]) scaled 0.75 (≈0.85 m tall) with a 'cap' accessory and two mitt spheres at the deck. Keep kidBody/kidArms as the bounce and arms groups so animate() still works: bounce the blob's y, and swing two small mitt spheres on .2 m arm stubs. Remove the skin and hair spheres. Keep its solid at station.ts:232.
findings.verify: Retake arcade-models-35 and -33: only Pip and blobs on screen. Grep `#f2c49b` in src/stations returns nothing. tests/station-arcade.spec.ts passes (the kid is visual only).
findings.verify_reason: station.ts:225-231 builds cylinder legs and torso, a '#f2c49b' skin sphere head and a brown hair cap. In arcade-models-35 a peg-person kid with skin head and brown hair stands by the pink cabinet, with the yellow stripe box on its back. It breaks DR-60, but it is an art-style issue that does not affect play or teaching, so P2.

findings.title: Beanbags still read as macarons or stacked jelly lobes, the arcade's most common clutter shape
findings.problem: prefabs.ts:130-137 builds the beanbag from a squashed sphere (r .45, y-scale .48), a second squashed sphere for the back (r .34, scale 1.12/.72/.78), a dark torus seam and a flattened dark disc. From the game camera and especially from above (shots -07, -58), each is a two-tier rounded cake or macaron in candy pink, yellow, mint, lilac or sky, the same hues as the blobs. The arcade uses the `lounge` recipe 3 times of 8, plus `reading` (arcade.ts:155), and 3 level beanbags (arcade.ts:139), so there are about 25 of these lumps on the floor (survey -02). The seat dimple and seam are not visible at the game camera. ART F5 reported this and it is still open (P5 'bread loaves').
findings.fix: Rebuild 'beanbag' as one pear-shaped sack from a LatheGeometry profile (radius .44 at y .12, .40 at .25, .30 at .45, .18 at .58, bevel to the top), rotated so the tall back side leans 15°. Add a deep seat dent: a flattened sphere of the darker shade at y .40, offset forward .08, scale (1,.25,.9). Add 3 vertical seam lines: thin TubeGeometry curves r .008 in the darker shade, running from the top knot to the base. Add a small top knot/handle cylinder. Use 24+ segments. Lower the saturation 15% (offsetHSL(0,-.15,0)) so the shape doesn't share blob hues.
findings.verify: Retake arcade-models-58 (top-down) and -57: a first-look naming test says 'beanbag' or 'sack chair', not 'macaron', 'cake' or 'blob'. Squint test at the game camera (arcade-models-01).
findings.verify_reason: Arcade-models-58 (top-down) shows two-tier rounded pink, mint and sky lumps that read as macarons. The recipe uses lounge 3 times of 8, plus reading (arcade.ts:29), and 3 level beanbags (arcade.ts:13). The prefab is at prefabs.ts:130+. It breaks DR-52 (model detail), so P2.

findings.title: REGRESSION / still open: the STOREROOM plaque floats in mid-air over the doorway and has no thickness, so it vanishes edge-on and from behind
findings.problem: room.ts:115 creates `PlaneGeometry(1.5,.36)` at (-7.6, 2.1, 2.8) with rotation.y=0 and no backing, post or lintel. The doorway it labels is the gap between store-a's end (x -8.6) and store-b (x -6.55), so there is nothing under or behind it. From the default camera it hangs at head height in front of the west-wall cabinets (shots -14, -53). It hides the lower half of the PONG cabinet and is cut by the HUD (shot -01). Because it is a single-sided plane, orbiting 180° makes it disappear (shot -15). From the side it is an invisible sliver (shot -83: camera east of the storeroom, sign not visible at all). This breaks DR-72 (nothing floats), DR-49 (mounted signage only) and DR-63 (no open-backed planes). ART F8 reported it.
findings.fix: Build a doorway frame: two posts rbox(.12,2.25,.3) in the CAP colour at (-8.55,1.125,2.6) and (-6.6,1.125,2.6), and a header beam rbox(2.07,.22,.32) at (-7.575,2.2,2.6), all as solid() so props collide. Mount the plaque on the beam's +z face at z 2.6+.165 as a 1.5×.3 rbox(…,.03) GRAPE board with the text plane 5 mm proud. Add a second text plane on the −z face (rotated π), so it reads from inside the storeroom. Lower the y to 2.2 to stay under the cutaway view.
findings.verify: Retake arcade-models-14, -15, -83 (orbit 0/90/180): the sign is seen mounted on a beam over the doorway from every angle, and readable from both sides. g.audit(.02) still shows 0 overlaps with the new solids.
findings.verify_reason: room.ts:115 is a bare PlaneGeometry with flat(), and flat() is a FrontSide MeshBasicMaterial (render/kit.ts:61). Nothing mounts it. findings.title: Claw machine tell overlaps its own cabinet: the glass case swallows the deck and hides the screen, so two machines are merged into one muddy silhouette
findings.problem: room.ts:89 places the claw group at local z .8 on the CLAW cabinet. The base box .9×.9×.8 spans local z .4..1.2, and the glass box(.84,.8,.74) at y 1.3 spans y .9..1.7, z .43..1.17. The cabinet's control deck rbox(.97,.08,.5) at y 1.2, z .25 spans z 0..0.5, so the deck pokes 7 cm into the glass volume. The glass sits directly in front of the cabinet's screen (head screen at y ≈1.56), so at the game camera the CLAW cabinet shows a pale translucent box over its screen (shots -21, -59, -80). The claw itself is a single 1.2 cm rod (cyl(.012,…,.3)) with no gantry or grabber, and the glass has no corner posts or top, so the toon outline traces a ghost box. It reads as 'an upright cabinet with a fish tank glued to it', not a claw machine.
findings.fix: Make the claw cabinet a proper claw machine instead of a tell glued onto an upright. For j.id==='claw', skip the standard head, screen and deck, and build: base cabinet rbox(.95,.9,.85) in body colour; a glass case of 4 corner posts box(.04,.9,.04) in PLUM plus 4 glass panes (opacity .3) spanning y .9..1.8; a top box rbox(.95,.25,.85) carrying the marquee; a gantry rail box(.8,.03,.03) at y 1.72 with a claw (cyl hub r .05, plus 3 bent prongs of cyl(.012) rotated ±.5); a prize chute window at the front bottom; and a joystick plus button deck rbox(.6,.06,.25) at y .95 in front. Move the prize balls to y 1.0–1.15 inside the panes. Keep the solid footprint .95×1.8×.85.
findings.verify: Retake arcade-models-21 and -80 at zoom 9 and the game camera: the silhouette reads as a claw machine (glass box on a base with a claw visible), and no part intersects (check via a bounding-box overlap script on the cabinet's children).
findings.verify_reason: The overlap math checks out. The claw group is at local z .8 and the glass box(.84,.8,.74) spans z .43..1.17 and y .9..1.7. The deck rbox(.97,.08,.5) at z .25, y 1.2 spans z 0..0.5 and y 1.16..1.24, so it sits 7 cm inside the glass volume (room.ts:64, 89). The visual claims are overstated. In arcade-models-21 the cabinet screen is still visible through the 35% glass, and the glass box of balls with the rod reads roughly as a claw machine.

findings.title: Handheld tell is a giant Game Boy hovering 12 cm in front of the cabinet with no bracket, covering the cabinet screen
findings.problem: room.ts:90 places the handheld group at local (0, 1.3, .6) with rotation.x -.2 and nothing between it and the cabinet. The cabinet body face is at z .4 and the deck's front edge at z .5, while the handheld's back face is at about z .54–.69 over its height. Seen from the side (shot -80) there is a clear air gap, with the Game Boy floating in front of the deck. findings.fix: Either mount it as a display: put the handheld on a stand (a PLUM rbox(.3,.06,.25) foot on the deck at y 1.24, z .3, with a back strut box(.06,.4,.04) rising to the handheld's back) and lower the group to y 1.55, z .35 so it sits in the deck recess. Or, better, replace the cabinet head with a 'handheld kiosk': a low counter rbox(.9,1.0,.6) with the handheld lying on a tilted cradle at 30°, tethered by a coiled cable (TubeGeometry helix r .012, INK) to the counter.
findings.verify: Retake arcade-models-80 (side, low) and -21: the handheld touches its mount (a gap under 1 cm), and the cabinet screen is either visible or intentionally replaced.
findings.verify_reason: Rotating the handheld (room.ts:90: group at z .6, rotation.x -.2, depth .12) puts its back face at z ≈.45 at the top and ≈.64 at the bottom. The cabinet body front is at z .4 and the head front at about .30, so there is a 10–15 cm gap with no mount. Arcade-models-80 shows the gap from the side.

findings.title: Pinball tell reads as a side table with three knobs, not a pinball machine; an office chair is parked in front of it
findings.problem: room.ts:87 builds the pinball 'table' as a flat rbox(.8,.14,1.1) with a dark top, 3 short pink cylinders and 4 thin plum legs, set flat (no incline) in front of an upright cabinet. findings.verify_reason: room.ts:87 builds a flat table with 3 knobs and 4 legs and no incline. In arcade-models-16 it reads as a small dark-topped table in front of the PINBALL upright, with a pink task chair from arcade.ts:12 (-7.8,-5) parked in front.

findings.title: The serviced cabinet's ribbon cable stops in mid-air on the bench as a loose purple stub that reads as a pen, never reaching the channel board
findings.problem: station.ts:222-223 builds the ribbon cable as a TubeGeometry from local (.35,.9,-.2) to (1.8,1.05,.5) in the cabinet group, which sits at (-2.95,0,-2.8) with ry .38. Its end is at about world (-1.09, 1.05, -3.0), lying on the bench top 1.1 m from the channel board (board centre at about (-0.08,1.08,-2.29)), and it ends in an open tube. In every bench-view shot (-36…-42, -78) a lilac 'crayon' lies on the bench behind the bins, connected to nothing (crop -36b). The station's premise is 'the broken cabinet's LED channel is opened up on the bench' (station.ts:1-3). The one physical link that shows the board IS the cabinet's circuit is broken, which hurts teaching (the player doesn't see that the board is inside the machine) and is a visible modelling error at the most-viewed camera.
findings.fix: Route the ribbon from the cabinet's open back to the board's SUPPLY edge. Compute the end point in world space as this.top.localToWorld(BOARD.x+SUPX-.1, .06, BOARD.z) and convert it into cabinet-local with c.worldToLocal. Use 5 control points: rising out of the cabinet back, a sag to y .99 on the bench top, then onto the board. Model it as a flat ribbon (ExtrudeGeometry of a .08×.01 rect along the curve, or a scaled tube with scale.z=.2) in GRAPE with 3 thin coloured stripe tubes. End it in a black IDC connector box(.1,.03,.05) plugged into a header on the board's left edge.
findings.verify: Retake arcade-models-36 (bench view): a flat ribbon runs from the serviced cabinet into a connector on the board's supply edge, with no loose end visible. Orbit shot -34 shows it continuous.
findings.verify_reason: Computed position: the cabinet group is at (-2.95,0,-2.8) with ry .38, so the tube end at local (1.8,1.05,.5) lands at world (-1.09,1.05,-3.00). The board centre is at (-0.08,1.0,-2.29), 1.2 m away. The open lilac tube end is visible on the bench in arcade-models-36b, arcade-models-35 and arcade-models-41 (left of the meter).

The alternative 'raise to y 1.75' at x 1.9 is wrong: the top edge reaches 2.31 and overlaps the plum neon board (room.ts:100, rbox 4.9×1.05 at y 2.45, so y ≥1.925 for |x|≤2.45). findings.title: Change machine and prize shelf are minimum-detail slabs (one 1.2 m² flat face with two decals; a cream box with balls)
findings.problem: The change machine (room.ts:104) is rbox(.8,1.5,.6) in SKY with a black screen box(.5,.3) and a yellow slot box(.3,.06). Its front is 0.8 × 1.5 = 1.2 m² of flat colour with 2 small cues, and the sides and back are blank. At the game camera it reads as a blue fridge or locker (shots -19, -20, -60). Prize shelf: make it a ticket-prize counter with a glass-front display (2 shelves inside, prizes sitting on them, opacity .3 front pane with PLUM frame), price tags (small cream planes with numbers), a top rail of plush prizes (blob-free shapes: a star, a rocket, a teddy-ish rounded box), and a 'PRIZES' plaque mounted on its front.

findings.verify_reason: room.ts:104-105: the change machine is one rbox with 2 small boxes on the front, and the prize shelf is one cream rbox with 6 spheres. Both have fewer than 6 cues and a flat face of about 1.2 m². Arcade-models-74 also shows the shelf as a plain box with balls.

findings.title: Clutter recipes overlap their own items (6 beanbag–paper interpenetrations at start), and 'lounge' is 37% of recipe draws, so identical beanbag+beanbag+plant triplets are copy-pasted across the floor
findings.problem: g.audit(.02) at start reports 6 overlaps, all beanbag vs paper at 3 cm: beanbag @(-1.22,-5.58)/paper (-0.72,-5.13); (0.43,-3.88)/(-0.07,-4.33); (2.67,-4.54)/(2.17,-4.99); (4.4,0.39)/(3.9,-0.06); (-5.29,1.63)/(-5.74,2.13); (1.14,3.41)/(0.69,3.91). The cause is clutter.ts: the 'lounge' recipe (clutter.ts:38) puts a beanbag at (.55,.15) and paper at (.1,.65). Their centres are 0.67 m apart, while the beanbag's half-diagonal is 0.636 and the paper's is 0.19. Placement (clutter.ts:83) only tests a cluster against previously placed props, never its items against each other. DR-70 wants zero overlaps at .02. Separately, arcade.ts:155 lists recipes ['lounge','crates','cones','reading','lounge','bins','crates','lounge']: lounge is 3/8 (37.5%) of draws and 'reading' adds more beanbags, over DR-67's 25% cap. The survey (-02, -43) shows the same 'two beanbags + plant' arrangement repeated about 8 times with only a quarter-turn, which reads copy-pasted.
findings.fix: (1) clutter.ts:38: move the lounge paper to (dx:.1, dz:.95) or drop it, and make the 'reading' paper dz .8. (2) clutter.ts:76-84: also test each item against the earlier items of the same cluster (skip pairs where one is stacked, y>.5), using rad_i + rad_j*.85 + .02. (3) arcade.ts:155: recipes ['lounge','crates','bins','reading','crates','arcadequeue','tickets','plants'], adding two arcade-specific recipes in clutter.ts: 'tickets' (a kraft box plus a spilled ticket-roll coil of 2–3 flat cyl(.08,.08,.06) in cream) and 'arcadequeue' (2 stools plus a mug plus a token cup). (4) Give each recipe a little random variety: jitter dx/dz ±.1, rotate the beanbags individually by ±.6 rad, and randomly omit one item at 30% chance.
findings.verify: `g.audit(.02)` returns [] for arcade (and for every level using lounge). Count recipe instances from the clutter output: no recipe exceeds 25% of clusters. Retake the survey arcade-models-02.
findings.verify_reason: g.audit(.02) called before any advance (v2.mjs) returns exactly the 6 beanbag-vs-paper pairs listed, each 3 cm deep. At .04 it returns []. clutter.ts:38 (lounge) and :76-84 test items only against `placed`, and items of the same cluster are pushed only after the whole cluster passes, so they are never tested against each other. Recipe draws: lounge is 3 of 8 (arcade.ts:29). Note that audit(.02) called after a 0.05 s advance already returns [], because physics separates them.
findings.fix_correction: The palette and recipe line is arcade.ts:29, not :155.

findings.title: Cardboard boxes are candy pink, mint, lilac and sky, and traffic cones are scattered through an arcade: prop colour families and semantics are broken
findings.problem: arcade.ts:135 makes storeroom boxes '#ffa6c9' and kraft alternately. The clutter colours (arcade.ts:155) feed every 'crates', 'cones', 'cart' and 'box' item, so most shipping cartons on the floor are pink, mint, lilac, sky or yellow, with parcel tape and labels (shots -01, -17, -21, -55). DR-51 requires cardboard to stay kraft. Pastel cartons merge with the beanbags, chairs and cabinets into one mid-value candy field, so nothing reads as a cluster (ART F4, F18). Traffic cones come from the 'cones' recipe, the fill pass ['box','box','cone','litter'] and two level cones (arcade.ts:141). About 12 orange cones stand in the middle of a carpeted arcade (shots -01, -51, -57), where they read as a construction site and add a hot orange accent that competes with the job marker. ART F18 asked for cones only as a cordon near the storeroom; still open.
findings.fix: (1) clutter.ts: let a recipe item opt out of the level palette. 'box' items always draw from FLOOR kraft ['#c98f5a','#d7a56d','#e0b47a']; only fabric kinds (beanbag, chair, sofa) take level colours. (2) arcade.ts:135: storeroom boxes all kraft. A pastel accent can live on the label (prefabs.ts:61 label colour) rather than the carton. (3) arcade.ts:155: remove 'cones' from recipes and 'cone' from fill (fill ['box','litter','bin']). Keep the two level cones only as a pair at the storeroom door with a wet-floor sign, or delete them.
findings.verify: Unit test over clutter('arcade') output: every 'box' colour is in the FLOOR set, and cone count ≤2. Retake arcade-models-01/-02; k-means on the survey: the top 3 clusters cover ≥70%.
findings.verify_reason: arcade.ts:9 makes storeroom boxes alternate '#ffa6c9' and kraft. The clutter colours (arcade.ts:29) feed 'box' items in crates, cones and the fill pass, and 'cones' is both a recipe and a fill entry. Arcade-models-01 shows pink, teal and sky cartons and about 10 orange cones on the carpet. This breaks DR-51.

findings.title: Players' 'stools' are office task chairs with five-star caster bases, parked in front of every cabinet
findings.problem: arcade.ts:138 places 10 'chair' props, commented as 'Stools', at the cabinets: one 1.9 m in front of each back-wall cabinet and one in front of each side-wall cabinet. Model it as a round padded seat cyl(.2,.2,.08) in fabric colour with a darker piping torus, a chrome post cyl(.03), a foot ring torus r .17 at y .3, and a weighted base cyl(.2,.22,.04) in INK, with 24+ segments. Use it in arcade.ts:138, placed 0.9 m in front of each cabinet's deck (z -5.9 for the back row) and turned toward it. Keep task chairs only at the desk (arcade.ts:143).
findings.verify: Retake arcade-models-51/-53: round stools at the cabinets. g.audit(.02) = [] after the move.
findings.verify_reason: arcade.ts:12 places 10 'chair' props at the cabinets, and the only chair prefab is the five-star task chair (prefabs.ts:66-76). Office chairs face the machines in arcade-models-16 and arcade-models-21.

findings.title: Lighting is over budget: 6 point lights at start (+1 on lightUp) and a neon glow sprite that grows to 8 m
findings.problem: A scene traverse (s2.mjs, scene.json) finds 6 PointLights at start: the bench lamp (0,2.7,-1.8, i 5); pink (-6.4,2.4,-5.4) and cyan (6.2,2.4,-5.4), both i 4; lilac (8.4,2.2,1.2) i 3.5; storeroom (-8.6,2.4,5.4) i 3; and the bench LED light (station.ts:172), which sits at 0 intensity until lit. lightUp() (room.ts:124) adds a 7th (i 8, distance 9). DR-66 caps this at 4 including light-ups (the known count was 5+1). The neon glow sprite is 5 m at opacity .18 (room.ts:100) and lightUp adds an 8 m sprite at .3 (room.ts:124) over a 4.6 m sign, 1.7× its source, against the ≤1.5× rule. In the win frames (-73, -74) the back wall washes pink. Each extra point light also multiplies the toon shader cost on ~650 toon meshes.
findings.fix: Keep 3 room lights: the bench warm lamp, one pink at (-4,2.4,-5.4) with distance 8, and one cyan at (5,2.4,-3) with distance 8. Fold the lilac and storeroom lamps into lampPool decals plus emissive cabinet screens. Make the bench LED's PointLight the 4th and only dynamic light. In lightUp(), raise the existing pink light's intensity instead of adding a new PointLight, and cap the glow sprite at 6.5 m (1.4×) with opacity .22.
findings.verify: Scene traverse after load and after the win: ≤4 PointLights. Retake arcade-models-74 and diff with ?bloom=0; the back wall keeps its cream value (median luma within 15 of the start shot).
findings.verify_reason: A scene traverse (v1.mjs) finds 6 PointLights at start: [0 (bench LED), 5, 4, 4, 3.5, 3]. Three.js counts a light in the shader even at intensity 0. lightUp() (room.ts:124) adds a 7th light and an 8 m glow sprite over the 4.6 m neon, 1.74× its size against the 1.5× cap. Arcade-models-74 does not clearly show the back wall 'washing pink' (the wall stays mostly cream), so that part is weak.

findings.title: Carpet floor is too dark for the value rule (median luma ~103 vs 140–185), and lilac props sit close in hue to the mauve carpet
findings.problem: PIL measurement on floor crops of the start shot gives median luma 102 at (900–1050, 520–600) and 105 at (560–700, 560–640), identical with ?norim (shot -76). The carpet base is '#6a5480' (room.ts:22). DR-54 asks for 140–185, measured from the concept floors. The arcade is intentionally moodier, but at this value the INK outlines (luma ≤70) lose contrast against the floor. Lilac boxes and beanbags (#9b7bf0/#c2b2ee, luma ≈135) differ from it by about 32 luma but sit close in hue, so they camouflage. The dark floor plus pastel clutter makes the room read as 'purple noise' in the survey (-02). The pastel props pass the ≥25 luma prop-floor difference.
findings.fix: Lift the carpet base to a dusty mauve around '#8f7aa6' (expected luma ≈135–145 under the arcade mood) and cut the confetti to 40 pieces at alpha .6 (room.ts:24-25). Or keep the dark carpet only under the cabinet rows (a 2 m band along the walls) and use a lighter '#a594b8' field for the walkable centre, which also frames the bench. Avoid lilac (#9b7bf0) on floor-standing clutter; use peach or sky instead.
findings.verify: PIL median on the same floor crops of a retaken arcade-models-01 falls in 140–185. Lilac props differ from the floor by ≥25 luma and ≥20° hue, or are removed.
findings.verify_reason: With PIL on my own retaken start shot (verify-arcade-models-01-start.jpg) I get floor-crop medians of 102 at (900,520,1050,600) and 105 at (560,560,700,640). The original shot and the norim shot give the same values. The carpet base is '#6a5480' (room.ts:22). DR-54 asks for 140–185, and DR-53 already lists the arcade carpet as a known fail.

findings.title: Block-pop smoke puff blankets the bench meter at the moment the player needs to read why it popped
findings.problem: popBlock() (station.ts:303) emits 8 'smoke' particles at the chain position plus 8 debris. From the bench camera, shot -41 (1.6 s after POWER on the claw cabinet with the 220 Ω block) shows a large translucent grey disc about 500 px across covering the whole meter screen and the board. The toast underneath explains '441 mW into heat (P = I²R)'. By shot -42 (0.8 s later) it has cleared, so the meter is obscured for at least several hundred ms right when the explanation is shown. DR-79 says effects never block the taught part for more than 0.3 s and smoke must not stack into solid balls. The popped block also simply disappears from the pad with a small debris burst; nothing physically pops off the board (A6 not built).
findings.fix: In popBlock(), emit the smoke at the board position with smaller particles: count 4, start scale .15 growing to .35, lifetime .6 s, alpha .5→0. Drift them away from the camera (−z, toward the back of the bench) and up, not toward the meter. Add a physical pop: spawn the block mesh as a short-lived tumbling object, launched up 0.6 m with a spin, that lands beside the board and fades after 1.5 s. Keep the meter untouched.
findings.verify: Capture the bench at +0.1, +0.3 and +0.6 s after the pop (extend s4.mjs). In the +0.3 s frame the meter's CURRENT and HOTTEST BLOCK tiles are fully legible (no smoke over the meter rect).
findings.verify_reason: popBlock() (station.ts:303) emits 8 smoke particles at the board. Arcade-models-41 shows a large translucent grey disc over the meter and the upper board. The meter text (CURRENT, CHAIN, POWER OFF) is still readable through it, so the harm is small. DR-79 is misquoted: its rule is about flashes ≤120 ms and not blocking Pip, not 'the taught part for 0.3 s'.

findings.title: Win push-in frames the bench meter's black 'ALL FIXED' screen and Pip cut at the frame edge, not the five cabinets that came alive; big confetti squares cover the shot
findings.problem: For stations, winFocus() (game.ts:398) is the bench table + 0.5 m, pushed in to 7 m at pitch .5 (game.ts:373). Shots -73/-74/-75 show the meter as a black panel with tiny 'ALL FIXED' text, Pip in the lower-left corner with feet cut off, and the result card over the right half. The payoff, five back-wall cabinets with lit marquees and screens, is off-frame (only the HANDHELD cabinet edge is visible at the right). At +0.15 s, cheer() confetti squares 60–100 px across fly through the camera and cover the meter and Pip (shot -73). DR-11 wants Pip and the working machine in the centre 70% of the frame. The A10 fix (no confetti through the bench camera) does not cover the win push-in.
findings.fix: Give Station an optional winFocus(). For the arcade, return the midpoint between Pip and the back-wall cabinet row (≈ (0,1.4,-5)), with distance 10 and the camera yawed so that the bench, Pip and the lit row are in frame (target offset to the left of the result card: right = −2.5). On win, also make the meter draw a big lit 'ALL FIXED' marquee (gradient, 120 px font) instead of black. In cheer(), spawn confetti beyond 2 m from the camera (cull particles whose distance to cam < 2) and cap the particle size at .08 m.

findings.title: Serviced cabinet base and body intrude 2–4 cm into the service bench; round props rest on box colliders
findings.problem: buildCabinet() (station.ts:215) places the serviced cabinet at (t.x+OX-2.75, 0, t.z-.35) = (-2.95, 0, -2.8) with ry .38. Its body corner (local (.475,.4)) lands at world x -2.361 and the PLUM base corner at x -2.33. The bench body starts at x -2.35 (W 4.3 centred on -0.2) and the bench top overhang at -2.40. So the cabinet body pokes about 4 cm into the bench top and the base about 2 cm into the bench body, at z ≈ -2.6 (visible as the cabinet edge melting into the bench in shots -34, -72). Both are fixed bodies, so g.audit can't see it. Separately, every prop gets a cuboid collider (game.ts:124), including the round beanbag, plant, bin, lamp and cone. Tumbled round props therefore rest on invisible box corners (DR-71), and the beanbag's 0.9 m box makes neighbouring props float 1–3 cm off its curved sides.
findings.fix: station.ts:215: move the cabinet to t.x+OX-2.85 (10 cm further left) or reduce ry to .3, and update the solid at :224. Better, add a fixed-vs-fixed check to audit() for station solids. game.ts:124: choose the collider by kind: beanbag → ColliderDesc.roundCylinder(.25,.4,.05); bin and plant → cylinder (half-height, radius .19/.26); cone → cone(.3,.25); lamp → a compound of a base cylinder plus a shade cylinder. Keep the masses.
findings.verify: Compute the cabinet's OBB against the bench AABB in a unit test (0 overlap). Throw test: knock 5 beanbags, bins and cones, advance(5), then zoom-9 crops show no hovering. Each round prop's lowest mesh vertex is within 1 cm of the floor or support.
findings.verify_reason: Computed position: the cabinet at (-2.95,0,-2.8) with ry .38 puts the body corner (local .475,.4) at world x -2.361, z -2.605. The bench top overhang (W+.1=4.4 about cx -0.2) starts at x -2.40 and spans y .94–1.01, so the body sits ~4 cm into the top. The plum base corner (local .5,.425) is at x -2.328, ~2 cm into the bench body, which starts at x -2.35 (station.ts:135-137). The cabinet's axis-aligned solid (x -3.45..-2.45) does not overlap the bench solid, so audit cannot see this. game.ts:124 gives every prop a cuboid collider, which breaks DR-71.
findings.fix_correction: If the cabinet moves, move the matching solid (station.ts:224) and the kid solid (station.ts:232) with it, since both are derived from t.x+OX-2.75. RAPIER's roundCylinder signature is (halfHeight, radius, borderRadius), so .25,.4,.05 gives the beanbag 0.6 m of height. Check the cone collider's centre offset against the mesh pivot.

notes.fun: Seen through the models, the arcade's set dressing is charming from the default camera. The neon sign, candy cabinets with tells (dance pad, claw balls, Game Boy, coin hopper), working cabinets with lit screens and the warm bench pool all give it a clear identity. Each signed-off cabinet lighting up its marquee, with a glow and confetti, is a good small payoff (shot -43). The fun is hurt by the room being inert. There is no cable, nothing chaotic is designed in, and the only physical beat is the tray carry, which looks broken because the tray tilts on edge (-32b). The win push-in lands on a black 'ALL FIXED' monitor instead of the row of revived machines (-74). The kid play-tester bounces and cheers nicely, but it is a human peg figure. A blob kid queue, as R4B suggested, would fit both the fun and the art rules.
notes.playability: Models create real camera problems. The 1.35 m storeroom half-walls and the 2.16 m cabinets are not occluders, so Pip disappears behind them on the tray route and among the right-wall cabinets (-50, -24, -52). At diagonal orbits behind a corner, neither shell wall cuts away and the camera shows only the outside of a 3 m wall (-81). The draw-call count has regressed to about 1500 (A13 was 1181), because the 12 cabinets and the 221-mesh bench are built into game.root unmerged. The host holds 60 fps, but low-end hardware won't. Note for anyone rerunning the captures: in ?manual mode the cutaway and fade lerps advance only once per render call, so shots need several advance(1/60) calls to settle (my scripts do 20). Unsettled single-advance shots can show false wall occlusion. g.audit(.02) reports 6 beanbag–paper overlaps from the lounge clutter recipe. No console or page errors in any script (all close() returned []).
notes.teaching: Two model issues weaken the teaching. The LED BASICS poster's formula and polarity strip is hidden behind the prize shelf (-19b), and the serviced cabinet's ribbon cable ends in mid-air on the bench (-36b), so the physical link that says 'this board is the cabinet's LED circuit' is missing. The bench itself teaches well through its models: candy-coloured blocks with real colour bands and values on top, brass bus bars for side-by-side pairs, an LED with a cathode flat that rotates when flipped, a PTC fuse disc that glows red and cools, hot blocks that go orange and red and smoke, and a transistor and coin wheel for the hopper. It is still the best close-up in the game (-36…-42, -78). The block pop has no physical 'pop off the board' (A6), and its smoke covers the meter at the moment the toast explains P = I²R (-41).
notes.clarity: The tray (#ff7eb6) uses the exact clutter pink, and job-yellow #ffd84d is scattered over clutter boxes, beanbags and chairs, so the job item doesn't stand out without the marker (-01, -10). A grabbable cable reel next to the tray in a cable-less room is a strong false affordance (-12). The floating STOREROOM plaque reads from the default yaw but vanishes edge-on and from behind (-15, -83). At the game camera the 'OUT OF ORDER' marquee text is a few pixels tall (-49b); the broken/fixed state reads only through dark vs lit marquee and screen. That works, but broken cabinets have no other cue such as sparks, tape or a flicker. The bench monitor text is crisp at the bench view.
notes.models: What works: the bench is chunky and rounded, with a clear supply → fuse → chain → LED → across layout. The candy resistor blocks are excellent (rounded body, colour bands, brass caps, value tag). Cabinets read as arcade uprights from the front, with marquee, tilted screen head, deck buttons and coin door. Desk, monitor, cart, bins, plants and the floor lamp are fine at the game camera. Outlines are present on all toon props, and the scene uses only MeshToonMaterial (667) and MeshBasicMaterial (109), with no Standard or Phong materials (DR-57 passes). What fails: cabinets have blank backs and 1.5 m² flat sides. The claw tell merges into its cabinet (the glass swallows the deck and screen). The handheld floats in front of its cabinet. The pinball reads as a side table. The change machine and prize shelf are slabs. Beanbags are macarons. The kid is a human. Cardboard is pastel. Office task chairs stand in for arcade stools. The storeroom stock bricks look like tray blocks. The serviced cabinet clips 4 cm into the bench. There are 6 point lights (+1). The carpet's median luma is about 103, below the 140–185 band. Pip's helmet 'cat-ear' ridge (DR-64) is still visible in crops -32b and -34; that belongs to the Pip owner.
